author: Mark Manson
description:
People are more likely to act a certain way when you label them as the kind of person who would. It's a subtle form of psychological influence that taps into our desire to stay consistent with how others see us.

From compliments disguised as favors to carefully crafted sales pitches, these tactics show up in everyday interactions more often than you might think.
title: Every Contractor Used This Trick on Me

Almost every sales pitch runs on the same handful of tricks, and marketers have been perfecting them for about a century. Drew and I trace them back to Sigmund Freud’s nephew, who sold America on cigarettes as women’s liberation and bacon as a doctor-approved breakfast. Then we get into how those tricks show up today, like the “free” massage that cost Drew six hours in a timeshare presentation, why nearly everything online comes in three pricing tiers, and the one line that can double a sales page’s results. Once you know these tricks, you’ll see them everywhere. The catch? Knowing how they work barely protects you.
